newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ABARE sees higher Australia gold output in 97.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ABARE sees higher Australia gold output in 97.

text.p: Australian gold mine production is forecast to rise by about 11 percent to about 304 tonnes in 1996/97 to June 30 from an estimated 272.9 tonnes in 1995/96 the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) said in its December Australian Commodities publication.
However, the Australian government's main commodity forecaster said the gold price was likely to fall to an average A$487 an ounce in 1996/97 from A$514 in 1995/96.
The price in U.S. dollar terms is expected to average $379 in calendar 1997 from $389 in 1996.
ABARE said the cause of the decline in gold prices after February reflected weaker investment demand for gold and sluggish fabrication demand at a time of stronger mine supply.

It said world mine production is forecast to rise by 5.6 percent in 1997 to 2,471 tonnes. "The bulk of this growth is expected to come from emerging gold producing regions - in particular South America and Southeast Asia," ABARE said.
Increased forward selling of gold by producers was also expected to boost supply.

"Forward contracts between producers and bullion banks result in accelerated mine supply as central bank stocks are initially sold on the open market and then later returned, with interest, from the producers' output," it said.
"It is expected that to secure margins, forward sales by Australian producers will increase in 1996/97, reflecting the subdued price outlook and increasing operating costs," it said.

"Producers are also expected to increase hedging following the rundown in their hedge positions earlier this year when the gold lease rate increased to around 6-7 percent, up from the normal 1-2 percent," the report said.
